question: Directive 2023/970 on pay transparency aims to strengthen equal pay between women and men. It must be transposed by the Member States by 7 June 2026. Some of its provisions require companies to provide information on pay levels upon request from workers and to disclose data relating to pay gaps. Several Member States have already put mechanisms in place.

However, some of these preexisting national obligations differ significantly from the indicators set out in the directive, which complicates companies’ adaptation and risks generating additional compliance costs. Furthermore, in the current context, regaining competitiveness has made it essential to simplify the regulatory framework and reduce the burden on businesses.
In this spirit, the Commission has presented several omnibus packages aimed at easing certain obligations affecting our economies. 1.
Is the Commission considering including the Pay Transparency Directive in a future omnibus package?

Is the Commission considering introducing certain flexibilities for companies already subject to national obligations promoting equal pay, in order to limit their costs and allow for gradual adaptation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.6.2026) The Commission does not intend to include the Pay Transparency Directive1 in any future omnibus regulatory simplification package, as it considers the Directive to be essential for the full realisation of the right to equal pay between men and women.

The Pay Transparency Directive introduces proportionate pay transparency obligations, with reporting dates and periods that vary depending on the size of the companies2. It also provides flexibility concerning methodologies to guide the assessment and comparison of work of equal value by employers3 and allows the use of administrative data to assist companies in fulfilling their pay reporting obligations4.

To facilitate the implementation of the Directive, the Commission has held implementation workshops with Member States and social partners, covering all of its provisions. The Commission has also made funding available via the 2024 and 2026 Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values programme to support employers with pay reporting5.
Furthermore, the Commission and the European Institute for Gender Equality published an EU-wide toolkit to aid employers when carrying out gender-neutral job evaluations and classifications6.
1 Directive (EU) 2023/970 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 to strengthen the

application of the principle of equal pay for equal work or work of equal value between men and women through pay transparency and enforcement mechanisms. 2 Articles 9(2), 9(3) and 9(4) of Directive (EU) 2023/970. 3 Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2023/970. 4 Article 9(8) of Directive (EU) 2023/970. 5 https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/calls-forproposals?
